citation.title: Beyond Bar and Line Graphs: Time for a New Data Presentation Paradigm
citation.authors: Weissgerber TL, Milic NM, Winham SJ, Garovic VD

topic: Figure practices for continuous data in small-sample physiology studies
own_question: How do top physiology journals present continuous data? Do bar and line graphs of mean ± SE hide the data distribution?
actual_method_and_evidence: Systematic review of 703 physiology articles published January to March 2014. Bar graphs appeared in 85.6% of articles, most showing mean ± SE. Univariate scatterplots appeared in 13.4%. Constructed example datasets show that different distributions can produce the same bar graph. The authors recommend scatterplots and supply Excel templates. The work involves no fusion, tokamak, nowcasting or time series.
validation_if_relevant: Not relevant. This is a literature review, not predictive validation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite it for anything about plasma physics, CES, BES/ECEI or nowcasting performance.
Do not claim it shows that mean-only error summaries are invalid for our estimator comparisons.
Do not generalize physiology publication practices to fusion literature.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude from the intro and theory sections. At most, it could support a methods or figure note: show per-shot or per-sample error distributions, not only mean ± SE, and mark paired comparisons across estimators.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
